paragraphs: Eben o sela shechashab alehem mibbeod yom liptzoa bahem egozim usheqedim beshabbat "p shello yichadam lekak beperush ella raq bemachshaba lebad, vegam yichadam leshabbat zo bilbad, hare zeh muttar letaltelam lekol tzerakayv, lepi shehaeben o hassela darkam bekak ureuyim lehityached lekak leolam, lepikak day lahem bahakana qalla, dehaynu bemachshaba leshabbat zo bilbad. veim nishtammesh bah tashmish zeh mibbeod yom apillu paam achat bilbad - hukena lekak "p shello chashab aleha leshabbat zo, meachar shennishtammesh veasa maaseh; abal eben o beqaat etz shechashab alehem mibbeod yom lekassot bahem pi hechabit, kevan delav orechayhu behaki, en machshabto moelet kelum; vaapillu im kebar nishtammesh bahem tashmish zeh peamim rabbot bechol, apillu hake, kevan dela yichadam beperush letashmish zeh leolam lekassot bahem pi hechabit vekayyotze - asur letaltelam beshabbat; abal im yichadam bepiv beperush letashmish zeh leolam, az yarad alehem torat keli, meachar shennityachadu letashmish zeh leolam.

Mihu, im yichadam letashmish zeh leshabbat zo bilbad velo leolam, en zeh morid alehem torat keli, ella im ken asa bahem maaseh shel tiqqun shemmokicha dehem mukanim veomedim lekak, deaz muttar letaltelam letzorek oto dabar shehukenu lo, abal lo letzorek acher. lepikak, otam hannotenim beereb shabbat abanim o lebanim sebib haqqedera shel hachammin sheyyoklu beshabbat, tzarik leyachadam bepiv beperush leolam, ubechol yatzniem veyishmerem bemaqom acher kede lehishtammesh bahem tashmish zeh, veaz muttar letaltelam beshabbat beet shemmesir haqqedera meal hakkira. vetzarik lehazhir bazeh et baale-battim bedabar zeh, sheyyishmeru et haabanim veyihyu meyuchadim lekak bekol ereb-shabbat, velo yizrequm im abanim sheyyesh lahem bechatzer veyiqqechu bekol ereb-shabbat meabanim shebbechatzer min habba beyadam.

clarification.explanation: A stone one thought about before the Sabbath, to crack nuts with it on the Sabbath, may be handled (even without explicit designation, merely by thought), since a stone is by nature always fit for this; and it suffices to have thought about it for this Sabbath alone, and even one actual use before the Sabbath suffices. But a stone not naturally intended for this (such as one for covering the mouth of a barrel) is not sufficiently designated by thought alone, and must be explicitly designated permanently in order to acquire "the status of a utensil"; designating it for this Sabbath alone does not suffice unless one performed an act of preparation on it. Therefore, stones placed around a pot of cholent should be explicitly designated permanently and kept in a separate place during the week.
takeaways: A stone or rock always used for a certain action (like cracking nuts) requires only a thought for this Sabbath
An object not naturally intended for use needs explicit permanent designation to be considered a "utensil" permitted to handle

paragraphs: Nesarim haomedim lebinyan, im hecheliqam birhitani asur letaltelam, deqaped alayhu shello yitlakleku im yishtammesh bahem, velaken muqtzim hem; abal im lo hecheliqam birhitani, shari letaltelam. umihu, im maqpid alehem shello lehishtammesh bahem pen yitaqqemu veyitqalqelu, kegon shehem qallim vachashubim, az apillu lo hecheliqam birhitani, asur letaltelam, veim chashab alehem mibbeod yom lehishtammesh bahem, muttar; veayyen acharonim za"l.

clarification.explanation: Boards intended for building: if they have been smoothed with an adze (and one is careful that they not get dirty), they are muktzeh and may not be handled; if not smoothed, they are permitted. But if one is careful about them out of concern that they might warp (such as light and valuable boards), they are forbidden even without smoothing, unless he thought about using them before the Sabbath.
takeaways: Smoothed building boards (or ones a person is careful about) are muktzeh; unsmoothed, unimportant ones are permitted

paragraphs: Kol dabar metunnap kegon qy o tzoa, ben shel adam, ben shel tarnegolim vekayyotze: im hem bemaqom sheyyosheb sham, o bechatzer shenniknas veyotze beoto maqom, muttar lepannotam lehotziam laashpa o lebet-hakkisse apillu beyadayv mammash, vezehu hanniqra bedibre chaza"l bekol maqom "gerap shel rei"; veken im hu kemaboy bimqom derisat haregel, muttar lesalleqam litzdadin kede shello yetannepu bahem; abal im munnachim bemaqom sheeno yosheb vedar sham, veken im hem bechatzer sheachore habbayit, shehu maqom sheen niknasim veyotzeim bo veen maqpidim alayv im yesh bo tinnup, asur lepannoto mishsham beshabbat. veim yare mippene hattinoq shello yelek shamma veyitlaklek betzoa, muttar likpot aleha keli. velaken im yesh bechatzer ezeh chadarim sheeno dar bahem beshabbat, vegam en lo kenisa vitzia sham, veezdammen shenniknas sham tinoq vetinnep, asur lepannot hattinnup hahu beshabbat. veken bimot haqqayitz asher yoshebim vishenim al haggag, ubabboqer achar zerichat hachamma yoredim lematta, veen olin sham ad hallayla; veezdammen shehattinoq tinnep sham babboqer beet shehem yoredim - lo yipnu hattinnup ad hallayla kesheyyaalu yaan ki bayyom en olin sham mechamat chom hashshemesh, veken kayyotze bazeh.

clarification.explanation: Filth (vomit, excrement) in a place of habitation or a passageway may be cleared to the trash or the outhouse even with bare hands ("a chamber pot of excrement"). In a public passageway, it may be pushed aside. But in a place where no one lives and no one is careful about its cleanliness (an unused room, a back courtyard), it is forbidden to clear it away on the Sabbath; if there is concern regarding an infant, it is permitted only to cover it with a vessel. Likewise, in summer, when people sit and sleep on the roof and come down in the morning and do not go back up until night — if an infant soiled the roof in the morning as they were coming down, they should not clear the filth until night when they go back up, since during the day they do not go up there because of the heat of the sun; and so in all similar cases.
takeaways: Filth in a place of habitation or passageway may be cleared even by hand
Filth in an unused place may not be cleared; covering with a vessel (to protect an infant) is permitted
A place used only at night (a summer roof) is treated, during the day, as an unused place, and filth is not cleared there until people go back up

paragraphs: Gerap shel rei veabit shel me-raglayim sheshshopekim laashpa o lebet-hakkisse beshabbat, lo yachazirem limqomam reqanin, "p shemmachaziram kede sheyyipnu bahem od, lepi shehem atzman meusim vaasurim betiltul. ketzad yaaseh? achar sheyyishpekem bebet- hakkisse yitten bahem sham mayim, veaz muttar letaltelam ulehachaziram limqoman mippene shehammayim shebbetokam reuyim labbehema, deheqellu betiqqun zeh mippene sheddabar zeh yesh bo kebod habberiyyot. veha detzarik tiqqun zeh shel simat hammayim, haynu im silleq zeh haggerap miyyado keshehiggia laashpa o lebet-hakkisse, abal im shepako vehu odennu beyado, muttar lehachaziro "p shello hinnicha bo mayim; vezehu mishshurat-haddin, abal tob lehachmir lehannicha bo mayim "p shello silleqo miyyado.

clarification.explanation: A chamber pot or bedpan that was emptied into the trash should not be returned empty to its place (it is repulsive and forbidden to handle). The solution: put water in it before returning it (the water is fit for animals, and therefore it is permitted to return it, out of respect for human dignity). This applies if the vessel left his hand; but if it is still in his hand, it is permitted to return it even without water, and this is the letter of the law; but it is good to be stringent and put water in it in any case, even when the vessel was not put down.
takeaways: An empty soiled vessel should not be returned without water inside (unless still in one's hand, in which case it is permitted by the letter of the law)
Even when permitted by the letter of the law to return it without water, it is good to be stringent and add water in any case

paragraphs: En osin gerap shel rei lekattechilla, dehaynu shemmebi lepanayv dabar sheachar shaa o yoter yimas, vesomek bedato sheyyotziennu meachar shennimas venaaseh gerap shel rei. veim abar veasa lekattechilla addata dehaki, apillu hake muttar lo lehotzio aach"k kesheyyimas. veim yesh becheder acher sheeno dar bo, dabar shennimas venipsad mechamat haggeshamim sheyyoredim alayv, hittiru lo lekattechilla sheyyabi leoto cheder mittato lishkab aleha o shulchano leekol sham, veal yede kak yotzi oto dabar hannipsad venimas mechamat haggeshamim, ki titonen dato alayv mippene hammeus, vahava lah din gerap shel rei; vedavqa im yashab sham yeshibat qeba, kegon shemmaknis mittato lishkab o shulchano leekol sham, abal im raq yikkanes beatzmo derek aray veyomar: mah maus alay, veotziennu! lav, deomerim lo: lek mikkan lemaqom acher! kevan demittechilla lo haya yosheb sham; mah sheen ken im hiknis mittato o shulchano, en omerim lo: totzi shulchaneka vetelek mikkan lemaqom acher!

clarification.explanation: One should not create "a chamber pot of excrement" as the primary practice — that is, deliberately bring something repulsive so as to be permitted to remove it; if one already did so, it is permitted after the fact to remove it once it has become repulsive. It is permitted to bring a bed or table into an unused room containing something that would be damaged by rain, in order to be able to remove it from there — provided he sits there regularly and not merely for a brief visit.
takeaways: One should not deliberately create a situation of "a chamber pot"; but regular use of a room (a bed/table) permits removing something that became repulsive there

paragraphs: Maknis adam melo quppato apar mibbeod yom umannicho bebeto beqeren zavit asher meyached otah lazeh, kede laasot tzerakayv beshabbat beapar zeh, lekassot bo tzoa o dabar maus. vekol zeh davqa im meyached lo qeren zavit, sheaz hu nikkar shehu mukan veomed lekak, abal im hinnicho beemtza beto lemidras raglayim, batel hu legabbe qarqa habbayit, umuqtzeh hu veasur letaltelo beshabbat. vekol adam sheyyesh lo banim qetannim sheddarkam letannep bechatzer, yargil bedabar zeh, lehakin heapar beopen zeh; lepikak perot hattemunim bechol, muttar letallam mishsham beshabbat, sheen oto apar muqtzeh, shehare hekinu lekak mittechilla veyiched lo keli o qeren zavit, ubilbad sheyyihyeh heapar tachucha kol kak sheen bo mishshum asiyyat gummot.

clarification.explanation: It is permitted to bring dirt before the Sabbath and place it in a special corner of the house in order to cover excrement or filth with it on the Sabbath — provided it is designated for this in a particular corner (not placed in the middle of the house where people would step on it, in which case it is nullified into the ground and becomes muktzeh). For a similar reason, fruits buried in sand may also be taken out on the Sabbath, since the sand was prepared for this in advance and a vessel or special corner was designated for it, and it is not considered muktzeh — provided the dirt or sand is loose enough that removing the fruits from it is not considered the forbidden act of digging holes on the Sabbath.
takeaways: Dirt for covering filth on the Sabbath must be prepared in a designated corner in advance, not in the middle of the house
Fruits buried in sand may be removed on the Sabbath if the sand was designated for this in advance and is loose enough that removal does not constitute digging

paragraphs: Asur letaltel behema chayya veop apillu letzorek gupan o meqoman, mippene sheen reuyim beshabbat keshehem chayyim; velaken apillu op sherauy letzacheq bo hattinoq keshebbokeh, asur letaltelo; vp"k muttar likpot hassal lipne haeprochim kede sheyyaalu veyeredu bo, veen bazeh mishshum mebattel keli mehekano apillu shaa achat, lepi shebbeyado lehapricham miyyad keshealu alayv shello yaamdu alayv apillu rega, veachar sheyyaredu mealayv muttar letaltelo; mihu, im hayu haeprochim alayv kol meshek ben hashshemashot, asur letaltelo kol hayyom ap leachar sheyyaredu, demittok shehuqtza hassal venaasa basis ledabar haasur, huqtza lekol hayyom kullo. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" heeleti bs"d, dekol zeh davqa besal hamyuchad lahem middaat baal habbayit, abal im nizdammen shealu ben hashshemashot mealehem al keli o chepetz acher shello middaat bealim, lo neesar oto hakkeli; velo od, ella apillu im adam acher hinnicham sham bemitkavven - lo neesar, deen adam oser dabar sheeno shello, kevan sheasa shello middaat bealim, vekaasher niktob leqamman beinyan hammannicha maot al hakkar. vetzarik lehazhir et haam bikli hamyuchad laop sheqqorin bearbe "qapatz" (lul), deasur letaltelo.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to handle a live animal (livestock, a wild animal, poultry) on the Sabbath, even for its own use or its place, since it is not "fit" on the Sabbath while alive. It is permitted to place a basket in front of chicks so they can climb up and down from it, and this is not considered "disqualifying a utensil from its use" (since they can be chased away immediately). But if they remained on it throughout the entire twilight period, the basket becomes forbidden for that whole day (it becomes "a base for a forbidden object"). The Ben Ish Chai adds, from his book Makbetzal, that this law applies specifically to a basket designated for the chicks with the homeowner's knowledge; but if the chicks climbed on their own during twilight onto another vessel without its owner's knowledge — even if someone else deliberately placed them there without the vessel owner's knowledge — the vessel does not become forbidden, since a person cannot forbid an object that is not his own without his knowledge. By contrast, a coop vessel ("kefetz") specifically designated for poultry may not be handled under any circumstances.
takeaways: It is forbidden to handle live animals on the Sabbath under any circumstances

A basket that served as a place for chicks during twilight, with the owner's knowledge, becomes forbidden to handle for the whole day; but if they climbed on without the owner's knowledge (or were placed there by another), the vessel does not become forbidden
A coop vessel designated for poultry may never be handled, even when empty

paragraphs: Behema vechayya veop, medaddin otam birshut hayyachid, dehaynu sheochez betzavvaran ubatztzedadim lesayyean im tzerikim lekak mishshum tzaar-baale-chayyim; ubilbad shello yagbihem beinyan sheyyeaqeru raglehem min haqqarqa, demuqtzim hem vaasurim betiltul. veap al gab dehammuqtzeh asur bikhay gavna letaltel miqtzato - hittiru chaza"l ledaddot baal chayyim mishshum tzaar baale chayyim im hem tzerikim lekak; abal im en tzerikin lekak, asur ledaddot otam. vehattarnegolet, apillu im tzerika lekak asur ledaddot otah, mippene shehi magbahat atzmah keshemmedaddim otah, venimtza zeh metaltel et kullah, abal muttar lidchotah meachoreha beyadayim kede shettikkanes lallul im barecha mimmenna. velo hittiru ledaddot ella birshut hayyachid, abal birshut harabbim, vaapillu bekarmelit, asur ledaddot shum behema vechayya veop, gezera shemma yagbihem veyolikem; dela ameru "chay nose et atzmo" ella gabbe adam velo bebaal chayyim; umihu lidchotam meachorehem im barechu, muttar apillu birshut harabbim.

clarification.explanation: It is permitted to lead an animal along in a private domain (holding its neck and assisting it, out of concern for the suffering of animals), provided one does not lift it entirely off the ground. A chicken may not be led this way (since it lifts itself), but it is permitted to push it from behind. In a public domain, it is forbidden to lead an animal at all (a decree lest one carry it); but if animals have run off, it is permitted to push them from behind back to their place even in a public domain.
takeaways: Leading animals in a private domain (without lifting) is permitted out of concern for their suffering; a chicken may only be pushed from behind
In a public domain, leading is entirely forbidden, but pushing escaped animals back is permitted even there

paragraphs: Notel adam et beno birshut hayyachid, vehaeben o chatikat cheres beyad habben, vela chashib haab metaltel et haeben beyado. bammeh debarim amurim? kesheyyesh labben gaguim al abiv, sheim lo yittelennu – yecheleh, kelomar, yitztaer harbeh; vegam name dei epshar lehashlik haeben miyyad hattinoq, ki yitzaq veyibkeh, abal belav haki, asur litlo. vaapillu kesheyyesh lo gaguin alayv, lo hittiru ella beeben, abal im beyado dinar, asur littol hattinoq; vaapillu leechoz hattinoq bihyoto mehallek beraglayv name asur, gezera shemma yippol haddinar miyyado, veyishkach shabbat mechamat chashibut haddinar veyagbihennu, venimtza metaltel hammuqtzeh tiltul gamur.

clarification.explanation: A father is permitted to carry his son in a private domain even while the child holds a stone or a shard, and this is not considered the father handling the stone — provided the child has a genuine attachment to it (he would become ill or distressed if it were taken from him) and the stone cannot be removed from him without his crying. But if he is holding a coin, it is forbidden to take him at all, and even merely holding the child's hand while he walks on his own (without lifting him) is also forbidden, as a decree lest the coin fall and, forgetting it is the Sabbath, he pick it up.
takeaways: It is permitted to carry a child holding a stone (out of great distress), but not one holding a coin
With a coin in hand, even merely holding the child's hand while he walks on his own is forbidden, out of concern that the coin might fall and be picked up forgetting it is the Sabbath

paragraphs: Shakach meereb shabbat maot al hakkar o al machtzelet o al kisse vekayyotze, vetzarik hu lazeh hakkar beyom-shabbat lishkab alayv, hare zeh menaer hakkar, vehammaot nopelot sham; abal lo yetaltel hakkar im hammaot, vinaarennu bemaqom acher. veim tzarik lesheb bimqom hakkar, az muttar letaltel hakkar im hammaot shealayv lehannicho bemaqom acher kede lesheb sham. veim eno tzarik lo lekar velo limqomo, veraq choshesh al hammaot shello yigganebu, velaken rotzeh lepannoto mishsham o lenaaro, asur. bammeh debarim amurim? beshokeach, shello haya bedato qodem shabbat sheyyishshaaru sham beshabbat, ella haya bedato lahasiram mishsham qodem kenisat shabbat, veshakach velo hesiram, abal im hinnicham sham al daat sheyyishshaaru sham gam beshabbat, az naasa hakkar hahu basis laddabar haasur, vahare hakkar atzmo muqtzeh veasur lenaaro o letaltelo. vaapillu im abar venatal hammaot mealayv, apillu hake hakkar atzmo asur betiltul kedin shear muqtzeh sheasur lahazizo mimmeqomo. vekol shehaya ben-hashshemashot basis laddabar haasur, "p deachar ben-hashshemashot tekep netalo hammuqtzeh mealayv, neesar hakkar betiltul kol hashshabbat kullo, demittok dehuqtza ben-hashshemashot, huqtza lekol hashshabbat.

Vekol zeh benoten maot o shear muqtzeh al kar shello, abal im natan hammuqtzeh al kar shel chabero shello middaat chabero, eno neesar hakkar lihyot basis laddabar haasur, deen adam yakol leesor dabar shel chabero shello middato. vaapillu im ellu hammaot o shear muqtzeh hem shel baal hakkar atzmo, im kol zeh, kol shehu hinnicham shello middaat chabero, eno oser et hakkar veyakol lenaer et hakkar beshabbat im tzarik lakkar; veken yakol letaltel hakkar im hammaot lehannicho bemaqom acher im tzarik limqom hakkar; mihu, im hannacha zo shehinnicha hammuqtzeh al hakkar hayeta letobat chabero baal hakkar, yesh lehachmir, mishshum deamerinan, missetama nicha leh bedabar zeh, shehu letobato.

clarification.explanation: One who forgot coins on a cushion before the Sabbath: if he needs the cushion, he shakes it (the coins fall off) but does not carry the cushion together with the coins; if he also needs the place of the cushion, it is permitted to carry it, with the coins, to another place. If he needs neither the cushion nor its place, and is only worried the coins might be stolen, it is forbidden to handle it. All this applies when he forgot them (intending to remove them before the Sabbath); but if he knowingly left them there to remain through the Sabbath, the cushion itself becomes muktzeh (a base for a forbidden object) for the whole Sabbath. All this applies when placing the coins on his own cushion; but if he placed them on his friend's cushion without his friend's knowledge, the cushion does not become forbidden as a base for a forbidden object, since a person cannot forbid his friend's object without his knowledge — and this applies even if the coins themselves belong to the cushion's owner, as long as they were placed there without his knowledge: it is permitted to shake the cushion or carry it with the coins to another place as needed. However, if the placement was done for the benefit of the cushion's owner, one should be stringent, since it is reasonable to assume he would be pleased by it.
takeaways: Coins forgotten on a cushion: if the cushion is needed, one shakes it rather than carrying it; if placed there deliberately in advance, the cushion is muktzeh for the whole Sabbath
Placing a muktzeh item on a friend's cushion without his knowledge does not forbid the cushion (unless the placement was for the cushion owner's benefit, in which case one should be stringent)

paragraphs: Teba sheyyesh bah maot, asur letaltelah. veyesh mi sheomer: im hatteba meyuchedet lemaot, kegon teba sheqqorin bearbe "pashtekata" (quppa) apillu im silleq hammaot mimmenna mibbeod yom, asur letaltelah beshabbat; vehu haddin bekis hamyuchad lemaot, "p shehu haya reqam mibbeod yom, asur letaltelo. uletzorek gupam umeqomam, muttar letaltelam; vehu haddin im asa bahem ezeh maaseh vesilleqam min hayyichud hahu, muttar letaltelam. ulepi zeh, hu haddin bakkelub shel opot sheqqorin "qapatz" (lul), apillu shello haya betoko haop ben hashshemashot vehu reqam, asur letaltelo; abal letzorek gupo o meqomo, muttar.

clarification.explanation: A box designated for coins (such as a cash box) may not be handled even if the coins were removed from it before the Sabbath, because of its permanent designation. It may be handled for its own use or its place. The same applies to a poultry cage (a coop) — it may not be handled even when empty, except for its own use or its place. The same law holds if one performed an act removing them from that designation — then they may be handled.
takeaways: Vessels with a permanent designation for muktzeh use (a coin box, a coop) may not be handled even when empty, except for their own use or place

paragraphs: Teba shel chapatzim sheyyesh bah chapatzim shehem dabar hammuttar, veyesh bah maot gam ken: im hammaot iqqar shehem chashubim etzlo yoter min hachapatzim hammunnachim sham, asur letaltel hatteba; vehu haddin im haya chashibut haasur vehammotar apillu beshaveh bemishqal echad, gam ken asur letaltel hatteba; abal im chashibut hahetter etzlo yoter, muttar letaltel hatteba. veazelinan batar didda - vedabar sheeno chashub etzlo, "g dilgabbe acherim chashub, la miqqere chashub. veayyen "chayye-adam", kelal s"z, seip ' useip ch'; yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: A box containing both permitted items and coins: if the coins are more important to him than the items, it is forbidden to handle the box; if they are of equal importance, it is also forbidden; only if the permitted items are more important to him is it permitted to handle it. The measure is according to the importance of the items to that particular person himself.
takeaways: A box with both permitted and forbidden items may be handled only if the permitted items are more important to its owner than the forbidden ones

paragraphs: Im yesh batteba chapatzim shel hetter vachapatzim shel issur shemmuqtzim beshabbat, "p dachapatzim shel issur munnachim al chapatzim shel hetter, lo naasu chapatzim dehetter basis laddabar haasur; veim yitztarek beshabbat lachapatzim dehetter, yukal liqqach otam ulenaaram betok hatteba mecheptze haissur shealehem, yaan ki mah shemmannicha betok hatteba cheptze haissur al cheptze hahetter, lo haya lo bazeh tzorek ella kak nizdammen lo, veim haya mizdammen lehepek, sheyyihyu cheptze haissur lematta, lo ikpat lo; veen hahetter naasa basis ledabar haasur, ella im ken hinnicho alayv leezeh tzorek - ben letzorek haissur, ben letzorek hahetter. veayyen lehaggaon rabbenu zalman za"l, siman sh", seip ch', yeuyyan sham. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti, deim hayeta kavvanato shehinnicha cheptze haissur lemala, mippene shehu tzarik lahem tamid, sheyyihyeh nocha lo lehotziam ulehaknisam benaqel tekep umiyyad kol shaa sheyyitztarek lahem, vecheptze hahetter eno tzarik lahem, lekak hinnicham lematta - hinneh bazeh chashib hinnicham bekavvana letzorek, v"p shehu letzorek menuchat gupo, ubazeh naasu cheptze hahetter basis laddabar haasur, veasur lenaer cheptze hahetter kede leqachtam beshabbat. vetzarik kol adam lehashgicha bidbarim ellu bebeto, ki debarim ellu metzuyim hem.

clarification.explanation: A box containing both permitted items and forbidden (muktzeh) items together, even where the forbidden item lies on top of the permitted one — the permitted item does not become "a base for a forbidden object" if this arrangement happened incidentally (without special intention), and it is permitted to shake out and remove the permitted item. But if the forbidden items were deliberately placed on top (so they would be convenient to remove when needed), this is considered purposeful, and the permitted item beneath it becomes forbidden to handle. Every person should pay attention to such matters in his home, since they occur often.
takeaways: An incidental arrangement of a forbidden item on top of a permitted one in a box does not forbid the permitted item
A deliberate arrangement (for convenience in using the forbidden item) does forbid the permitted item beneath it
